description: We are Astra Pulse, building an interactive space game for kids for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. players manage a space base and balance life support, power, and radiation using real Nasa data.
summary:
Bahrain to the Moon is a free, browser-based 3D adventure game that teaches children the basics of programming through lunar exploration. Players choose one of four members of a Bahraini family (a programmer, an explorer, an engineer and a life-support specialist) and keep a Moon base running during emergencies.

Instead of reading long lessons, kids solve problems by building programs with visual coding blocks and pressing "Run Code". Their code changes the 3D world they can see: solar panels turn toward the Sun, the oxygen backup switches on, and the family moves into a radiation shelter during a solar storm. The three missions teach Sequence, IF/ELSE and problem-solving, and each one is grounded in real lunar science: solar power, life support and space-weather safety.

The game is important because it makes coding and space science feel exciting, accessible and culturally close to home for young learners in Bahrain and around the world. It runs on any laptop browser with no installation.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Bahrain to the Moon is a third-person 3D educational game for children and beginner programmers. A Bahraini family arrives on the Moon to maintain a lunar base. The player explores the base, follows mission beacons, talks to family members and fixes emergencies with a visual block-programming interface.

THE THREE MISSIONS

1. Power Crisis (Sequence): the player orders three blocks (Inspect, Activate, Connect). The program actually runs step by step. If the order is wrong, the exact failing step is explained. When it's right, the solar panels rotate to the Sun, energy flows to the batteries and the base lights turn on.

2. Oxygen Emergency (IF/ELSE): the player builds an IF/THEN/ELSE rule that is automatically tested at five oxygen levels. Logically equivalent answers are accepted, and distractor blocks give targeted hints. The backup system uses some power, which teaches trade-offs.

3. Solar Storm (Problem-Solving & Safety): the player chooses four safe actions out of seven and puts them in a safe order. The family then shelters from radiation until the storm passes. The game makes clear that a storm cannot be "stopped", only planned for.

After each mission, a success screen explains what happened, why the solution worked and the coding concept behind it.

FREE PLAY & REPLAYABILITY

Players earn stars by solving missions and a "Code Output Quiz" (variables, loops, if/else). They can mine glowing moon rocks with an upgradable pickaxe, drive a lunar rover over craters, hatch an alien pet companion, and travel through a Galaxy Portal to bonus zones on Mars, Saturn and Neptune.

IMPACT & CREATIVITY

Children learn by doing: mistakes are never punished, hints get more helpful with each try, and the code visibly changes the world. The family characters (from Manama, Muharraq, Riffa and Awali) give young learners in Bahrain role models they can relate to.

TOOLS & TECHNOLOGY

JavaScript (ES modules), HTML5, CSS3, Three.js (WebGL 3D rendering) and Vite. All 3D models, textures and sound effects are generated in code, so the game has no external art assets. It runs in any modern browser with no installation and is hosted on GitHub Pages.
